chunks: From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a fly that falls into oil, ghee, and food, so he said, 'There is no harm; eat it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on food contaminated by a fly?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the permissibility of consuming food contaminated by a fly without removing it, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the fly's body is not inherently impure (*najis*) in a way that necessitates removal for consumption. This ruling underscores the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) regarding the purity of common foods, distinguishing between minor impurities that do not alter the food's essence and those that do. It highlights the practical ease (*rukhas*) granted to believers in daily sustenance, provided no significant change in taste or quality occurs.
